elections.description: Congress won almost three-quarters of the elected seats in the first Lok Sabha general election, with less than half of valid votes nationally.
elections.note: Early elections included multi-member constituencies. The denominator is elected seats, rather than the number of constituencies.

elections.description: Congress increased both its seats and its valid vote share, retaining a large parliamentary majority.
elections.note: The elected-seat total rose from 489 to 494. Seat share accounts for this change.

elections.description: Congress retained its third consecutive Lok Sabha majority, despite a lower seat total and vote share than in 1957.
elections.note: National vote share and the share of constituencies won answer different questions.

elections.description: Congress lost 78 seats compared with 1962. It retained a Lok Sabha majority with a much smaller share of the elected seats.
elections.note: Outcome labels describe the election result, rather than every subsequent change during the parliamentary term.

elections.description: Congress regained seats and vote share, expanding its parliamentary majority after the reduced 1967 result.
elections.note: ECI lists Indira Gandhi’s Congress as INC and Congress (Organisation) separately as NCO. NCO is excluded from this series.

elections.description: Congress lost 198 seats compared with 1971 and moved out of Union government. Its share of elected seats fell below its national valid vote share.
elections.note: ECI records the leading Janata formation under BLD. Its result is separate from the Congress series.

elections.description: Indira Gandhi’s Congress returned with a majority, gaining 199 seats over the 1977 Congress result.
elections.note: This row follows ECI’s INC(I) label. INC(U) is a separate party and is excluded. The reported election covered 529 elected seats.

elections.description: The completed 1984–85 election cycle produced Congress’s highest seat total in this series.
elections.note: Combined cycle: 414 seats and 48.12% of valid votes, per ECI 2023. Initial 1984 count: 404 and 49.10%; deferred Assam and Punjab polls in 1985 added 10 Congress wins.

elections.description: Congress remained the largest party by seats but lost its majority. The completed-cycle comparison with 1984–85 shows a loss of 217 seats.
elections.note: ECI’s reported election-seat total is 529. Being the largest party did not itself establish majority support for forming government.

elections.description: Congress returned to Union government. The completed cycle increased its seat total over 1989, while its national valid vote share was lower.
elections.note: Combined cycle: 244 seats and 36.40% of valid votes. Initial 1991 count: 232 and 36.26%; deferred Punjab polls in 1992 added 12 Congress wins.

elections.description: Congress lost 104 seats against the completed 1991–92 cycle and no longer led the Union government.
elections.note: The ECI initial-1991 comparison gives a 92-seat loss. This edition uses the completed-cycle comparison consistently.

elections.description: Congress gained one seat compared with 1996, while its valid vote share fell by 2.98 percentage points.
elections.note: National vote share is measured across the reported election, not only in seats contested by Congress.

elections.description: Congress won 27 fewer seats than in 1998 despite a 2.48-percentage-point increase in valid vote share.
elections.note: This divergence illustrates why national vote gains do not guarantee more constituency wins. It does not identify a single cause.

elections.description: Congress gained 31 seats and returned to Union government through a coalition, despite a lower national valid vote share than in 1999.
elections.note: 145 is the Congress party total. UPA partners and outside supporters are not included.

elections.description: Congress gained 61 seats and increased its valid vote share, returning as the leading party of a coalition government.
elections.note: Congress’s 206 seats remained below the 272 needed for a majority in a full 543-seat elected House.

elections.description: A loss of 162 seats from 2009 brought Congress to its lowest Lok Sabha general-election seat count in this series.
elections.note: 19.52% is ECI’s valid-vote share. Figures using all votes, including NOTA, have a different denominator.

elections.description: Congress increased its tally by eight seats. The 0.15-percentage-point rise in valid vote share left it close to the 2014 level.
elections.note: PIB reproduces ECI’s table: 421 Congress candidates, 52 wins and 19.67% of valid votes. This differs from the all-vote share.

elections.description: Congress gained 47 seats from 2019. Its 18.23% share of elected seats remained below its 21.40% share of valid votes.
elections.note: ECI report 20 covers 542 contested seats; Surat was won unopposed by the BJP. Congress’s 99 is unchanged. Seat share here uses all 543 elected seats; alliance partners are excluded.
